purpose: Define a data-light but corpus-aware child workspace that can accept first real files and later-discovered corpus families without redesigning identity, authority, intake, work modes, lenses, providers or migration topology.
inclusion_rule: The ACR3 workbook migration inventory is one bounded migration source, not the complete corpus definition. Base shells must also retain the audited source-family registry, specialist-owner links, provider/runtime surfaces and unresolved Frontiers.
growth_rule: New project, agent, provider, tool, file type or source family can be added through the extensible registries and N-dimensional labels without schema replacement. If authority or placement is unclear, preserve source identity and create a Frontier.
payload_rule: Base shell contains corpus/source-family maps, current bounded control caches and migration metadata, but not bulk project workbooks/CAD/raw evidence until intake is explicitly reviewed.
hydration_rule: Use the latest verifier-valid descendant supported by the trusted seed lineage while retaining the distinct Recovery/promotion authority gate. Local/unbound implementation evidence must not be treated as a durable descendant until source, carrier and test receipts are persisted.
publication_rule: Portfolio, dossier, evidence review, Web2, social, email and institutional packages are generated representations/lenses and do not become source authority.
